_comment: Village banter (R7.2), merged onto data/dialogue/opening.json's table by dialogue_runner.gd. Same shape, same no-branching rule (see opening.json's own `_comment_shape`): a line or two per villager. `portrait` reuses trainer.png, the only generic human portrait art the project has; a bespoke portrait per villager is not part of this pass.
_comment_np3: NP3 (spec sec35) gave Mira, Oskar and Tam their named roles -- Meadow Keeper, Bridgehand, Field Scout -- as an opening identity line each, and added the Quarry Foreman and the Rescued Ranger as two new reused-rig villagers. None of the five offer a real fight: R8.1 (trainer combat) doesn't exist yet, so this is identity and foreshadowing only.
_comment_of30_effects: OF30 retires this file's original 'no `give:` or `beat:` effects -- these people have nothing to hand over' rule. Tam has something to hand over now. The effects work with no new plumbing on the panel side: `scripts/story/sequence_director.gd::_drain_effects()` drains the SHARED dialogue panel every frame and does not care which conversation is in it, and `scripts/world/village_npcs.gd` opens village lines on that very panel (through the `dialogue_panel` group). `beat:` is still forbidden here -- beats belong to the opening -- but `give:` and OF30's new `flag:` are not.
_comment_of30_tam: OF30 (owner: "Make one of the villagers a blacksmith who will give you a torch, an axe for trees and a pickaxe for stones. Then he'll give you the recipe for basic orbs."). `village_tam` stays exactly as NP3 wrote it and is still what Tam says on an ordinary greeting; the one-time handover is an ADDED branch, chosen by flag in data/config/village_npcs.json's `greeting_when`, not a replacement. Tam keeps the Field Scout identity: he is a smith who scouts, and the tools conversation opens by saying so. FIRST-HOUR-FUN moves the opening axe, pick and Basic Orb pattern to Mira's required first visit, leaving Tam's useful knife-and-torch follow-up intact. SC12 later adds his battle offer as a second entry in the same list. The torch line used to be narrative only -- OF24's carried torch was an always-on kit fixture, not an item, so there was nothing for a `give:` to name. OW12 changed that; see `_comment_ow12_torch_give` below.
_comment_ow12_torch_give: OW12 (2026-08-16) made the torch a real satchel item (items.json's `torch`, `kind: "tool"`) and retired the always-on kit fixture and the free-standing buildable both. That decision's own record, `docs/decisions/D53`, left the torch line here as words with no `give:` -- deliberately flagged as real, non-silent follow-up work, because nothing else in the game handed a `torch` out and the item would otherwise be permanently unreachable (`playground_hud.gd::_arm_torch_placement` refuses to equip one that is not in the satchel, and no other conversation offers one). That gap is closed here, in the same shipping pass: the 'take the spare torch off the wall' line now carries `give:torch:1`, on the same line as the words that already promised it, the same 'gift and flag/give together' shape the tool handover just above it already uses.
_comment_of30_knife: The owner named two tools ("an axe for trees and a pickaxe for stones") and the early route also needs a knife. item_db.harvest_yield()'s rule since R2.1 is right-tool = full, NO tool = half, WRONG tool = nothing, and `fiber` is gated on `knife` (items.json's `gathered_with`). A player carrying only Mira's axe and pick therefore owns 'some tool, just not that one' at every grass patch and gathers ZERO fiber. Tam's knife follow-up keeps the Basic Orb recipe's two-fiber cost achievable without changing that harvesting rule.
_comment_of30_flags: `flag:<id>` sets an autoload/progression_state.gd flag, the same store the road gate and the TM pickups already write to. `tam_tools_given` is what stops Tam's knife-and-torch handover repeating; `recipe_orb_basic` is what unlocks the Orb recipe in data/recipes/recipes.json (its `unlocked_by`). Both are set on the SAME line as the thing they record, so a conversation that is somehow cut short cannot bank the gift without the flag or the flag without the gift. FIRST-HOUR-FUN places the Orb lesson in Mira's required first visit instead of relying on a later optional greeting.
_comment_of31_trade: D39 (OF31, owner: "Make the villagers so I can trade with them. Creatures and materials... Make one of the villagers the merchant. He has a store in his house. He'll buy and sell goods from you. Make the third whatever makes sense."). Mira is the merchant and Oskar the creature trader; Tam stays the smith OF30 made him. Same additive shape as Tam's: `village_mira` and `village_oskar` are untouched and are still what each of them says on an ordinary greeting -- the trading lines are ADDED branches in data/config/village_npcs.json's `greeting_when`. The `shop:` effect is new (scripts/story/sequence_director.gd::_queue_shop) and reads `shop:<goods|creatures>:<vendor_id>`, where the vendor id is a key in data/config/trade.json. It opens the screen once the dialogue box has CLOSED, the same wait the starter picker already needed.
_comment_of31_coins: D39 chose the friendlier of the two starts the brief offered: Mira's first conversation hands over a float so the first visit to the shop can buy something, rather than a zero-start that has to be bootstrapped by selling. The count here and `starting_coins` in data/config/trade.json are checked against each other by tests/test_trade.gd -- a line that says thirty while the config says ten is a lie the player can count.
_comment_ow9_foreman: OW9 (owner: "Someone at the beginning needs to tell you to go gather materials to build things like orbs. Someone else will need to tell you to get wood and build a base camp. They should probably give you a hammer and recipe."). Mira's required first visit provides the gathering/Orb lesson; this is the build half, spoken by the Quarry Foreman -- the one villager with a trade that touches building and nothing yet to hand over. Second use of OF30's route exactly: one `give:`+`flag:` line, gated in data/config/village_npcs.json's `greeting_when` so it can never repeat. `hammer` is not a new item -- R2.1 shipped it as a real tool with nothing that gave it out yet (its own `_comment_tools`); this is that gift. There is no separate 'recipe' flag or item: `camp` (data/items/buildables.json) has never been locked behind an unlock flag the way `orb_basic` is -- GAME_DESIGN.md 20's mandatory tutorial shelter is meant reachable from minute one -- so gating the BUILDABLE would be inventing a system the design does not call for. The 'recipe' the owner asked for is spoken, the same way OF30 handed the torch over in words with no torch item: the Foreman names the materials a camp actually costs on the same line he hands over the hammer.
_comment_sc12_sc13: SC12/SC13. Mira, Oskar and Tam each gain a `_challenge` and a `_beaten` conversation, chosen by data/config/village_npcs.json's `greeting_when` once their vendor/gift branch is spent (spec sec3 Band 1, D39's dual-role rule). Every challenge's LAST line carries `battle:<trainer_id>` -- scripts/story/sequence_director.gd's fourth dialogue effect, read the moment the dialogue box closes, the same deferred-start contract scripts/world/trainer_npc.gd already uses for a standalone trainer. Mira's and Oskar's `_beaten` lines carry the exact same `shop:`/`shop:creatures:` effect their standing vendor branch always has, so the store/swap stay reachable forever once they are beaten (D39's rule made real); Tam's is flavour only -- he has no vendor effect left to carry.
_comment_r7_9: R7.9, owner-requested: an inn where the villagers can stay. Bram is its innkeeper, a THIRD vendor branch in the same additive shape OF31 gave Mira -- `village_bram_shop_intro` opens the store (`shop:goods:bram`, data/config/trade.json's own `bram` vendor: berries plus the three tonic/brew items, Mira's own prices) and `village_bram_shop` is the standing branch, chosen the same way in data/config/village_npcs.json's `greeting_when`. No starting-coin gift on his intro line -- Mira's `village_mira_shop_intro` already bootstraps the player's first purchase and a second float would be an unexplained windfall, not a kindness. D39's dual-role pattern also names a later trainer branch; this ships only the vendor half (see village_npcs.json's own `_why_vendor` on Bram's entry for the scope call and why).
_comment_hall_approach: SF34. The Meadows Hall approach gate (scripts/world/playground_world.gd::_build_sigil_gate). Nobody stands at this gate, so the words are a Team Tether notice bolted to the leaf — the same trick road_gate_locked plays with Grandpa's voice, but diegetic here rather than remote narration. The PORTRAIT IS A STAND-IN: the project has exactly two portraits on disk (grandpa, trainer) and neither is a faction notice; tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd requires a real one, so this uses the trainer plate under CLAUDE.md's Prototyping rule and should be replaced when the faction has art of its own. The sealed line never names how many Sigils are missing — the objective tracker counts (data/progression/objectives.json), and saying it twice in two voices is how a count drifts.

village_mira.speaker: Mira
lines: Meadow Keeper's what they call me around here — somebody's got to look after what grows out there, garden rows included. The meadow has opinions about strangers, mind.
That workshop's mended every tool this village ever broke. Still smells of iron and oak shavings.
Something's wrong with the ground out past the south crossing. Rows won't take there anymore — same seed, same season, and it comes up grey and thin. I've stopped trying.

village_mira_shop_intro.speaker: Mira
lines: Grandpa said you would come through. Take these before you head out: an axe for wood and a pick for stone.

lines.text: For Basic Orbs, bind three wood with two fiber. The pattern is yours now; make more whenever you need them. Elias left you fifteen to learn with.
Now then. I sell, and I buy — so if you're hauling wood and cut grass about the meadow, haul it here first.
Back again. Shelves are where you left them, and my prices haven't improved.

village_mira_challenge.speaker: Mira
lines: You've been kind to the meadow. So here's something it taught me: it pushes back.

lines.text: A keeper learns to stand her ground. Want to learn it with me? Nothing held back.
That was honest fighting. Stall's open whenever you need it.

village_bram.speaker: Bram
lines: Innkeeper's the whole of it. Bed, board and a fire that stays lit -- that's the trade.
Half the square eats here on a cold night. The other half just likes complaining about my stew where it's warm.

village_bram_shop_intro.speaker: Bram
lines: First one through the door gets the tour. Bar's here, beds are through the back, and I keep a bit of stock behind the counter same as Mira does.

lines.text: Berries, and the tonics and brews she doesn't always have spare. Have a look.
Back again. Shelf's the same as you left it.

village_oskar.speaker: Oskar
lines: Bridgehand's my trade — I keep the old crossing south of here in one piece, when it lets me. Team Tether's been sniffing round it lately, which helps nobody.
Well rope's been fraying since the spring thaw. Nobody's got round to it.
You're the one staying with old Elias, aren't you? Whole square knows by now.
They pay in coin and they pay on time, and I don't ask what the masts are for. Only — the verge by the south road used to be waist high. You've seen it.

village_oskar_trade_intro.speaker: Oskar
lines: Bridgehand's my trade, but I keep pens behind the cottage as well — creatures that came off the crossing road with nobody walking beside them.

lines.text: I don't sell them and I won't buy yours. Straight swap: one of mine for one of yours, and both of us shake on it. That's how it's done here.
One rule of my own, mind — I'll not take your last. Nobody walks back out to that meadow on their own. Come and see who's up.
Same terms as ever. Have a look at who's in the pen — they change about, so it's worth the walk.

village_oskar_challenge.speaker: Oskar
lines: That bridge south of here was mine to keep shut. Was. Tether took the key off my belt in the spring and put one of their own on the near landing.

lines.text: So I've nothing to hand you but a fight, and I'm told you're worth one. Come on then.
Square's square. Wish I still had that key to give you — the lad in the grey coat has it, down at the crossing. Mind the far bank either way. Nobody's walked it in years.

village_tam.speaker: Tam
lines: Field Scout, that's me — I track what's out there before it tracks you. Watch a creature's temper as much as its size; the placid-looking ones surprise you most.
Careful on the yard fence, the post on the end is looser than it looks.
Good road out to the meadow from here. Watch for the bramblebun, it startles easy.
Word of advice for out east: the grass by Tether's roadworks is dead flat and the creatures know it. Nothing dens within a hundred paces of those masts. I'd trust them over a surveyor.

village_tam_tools.speaker: Tam
lines: Field Scout when I'm out past the fence. Smith when I'm in. Same pair of hands either way.
You've been at the oaks and the outcrops with nothing but your hands, haven't you. It shows.

lines.text: Mira has you set for gathering. This knife and torch are for the work that runs long: clean fiber, then see your way home.

lines: Come back when they're blunt. I'll see to them.

village_tam_challenge.speaker: Tam
lines: Scouting teaches you one thing fast: no single creature answers every question.

lines.text: Bring your whole belt, not your favourite. I'll show you what I mean.

village_tam_beaten.speaker: Tam
lines: See? Right creature, right moment. Same craft as smithing.

village_quarry_foreman.speaker: Quarry Foreman
lines: Foreman by trade, though there's no quarry to run yet — Team Tether's been working the old rootstone seams south of here longer than anyone local has.
Give it time. Stone doesn't go anywhere. Neither do I.
You want the honest version? Every seam they've run a line off has gone bad above ground within the month. Grass first, then the scrub, then it's bare. They tell me that's the weather.

village_quarry_foreman_hammer.speaker: Quarry Foreman
lines: No quarry to run leaves a foreman with time on his hands. Enough to watch you crossing this square with an armful of deadwood and nowhere under a roof to put it down.
Wood left in a heap too long swells and rots on you. A trainer left out in the open does worse. Neither keeps well that way.

lines.text: Take this — my old hammer. No use to me without stone to cut. Get enough wood together, stone too if the trip's worth it, fiber for the binding, and you've a fire and a roof both. Simplest thing any of us ever raised.

lines: Don't put it on the road itself. Learned that one the hard way.

village_rescued_ranger.speaker: Rescued Ranger
lines: Ranger, before Team Tether had other plans for me. Took some doing to get clear of them — I'm still finding my feet.
Whatever you're chasing out there, watch the Tether patrols. They don't take kindly to company.

village_rescued_ranger_home._comment: SE27/SG46 (spec §14). What she says once she has walked here on her own feet, in a square where the player is the reason she can. Deliberately does NOT repeat the testimony — she gave it once, at the relay, and a villager who recites the plot every greeting is how §32's ladder turns into a wall of text. She restates only what the player can now ACT on (the crossing is open, the line goes on north) and otherwise gets on with being a person in a village. Still names no legendary and no power source: she does not know, and she does not learn it by moving house.
village_rescued_ranger_home.speaker: Sela
lines: Sela. I got here — and I've eaten, and slept indoors, and neither of those was true a week ago.
The mill crossing will hold once that gear's back in it. Go and see for yourself; I'd rather it was walked on than trusted.
I'm writing the survey up properly while I still remember the numbers. When you get further up that line than I did, come and tell me what you found. I'll believe you.

road_gate_locked.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: That gate's locked — has been for a while. The key won't be far from it, if you look.

road_gate_unlocked.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: There you go. The old key still turns.

hall_approach_sealed.speaker: Team Tether Notice
lines: APPROACH SEALED BY ORDER OF THE WARDEN. Three regional Sigils are required at this gate and no fewer.
The lock reads all three or it reads none. Two of the discs sit dead in your hand.

hall_approach_opened.speaker: Team Tether Notice
lines: Field. Ridge. Riverwatch. Three discs go into the plate and stay there.
The leaf swings back off the road. Meadows Hall is up the rise, and nothing is between you and it now.

village_mira_road._comment:
T5-STORY-2. Mira's MID-CHAPTER branch, and the first line anyone at home says about the war between the tournament and the Warden. Measured gap: tools/_probe_story_drive.gd walked the chapter's flags against a live village and every NPC said the identical thing at every rung from the tournament to the ending -- `village_mira_shop_intro`, `village_oskar_trade_intro`, `village_bram_shop_intro`, `tournament_halda_champion`, unchanged for the whole back half. MEADOWS_EXIT_CRITERION F3 is 'home stays relevant ... returning is worth it', and returning was worth exactly one repeated sentence.

Gated on `captive_rescued` because that is the beat that physically sends someone home: Sela's own last line in data/dialogue/relay.json is 'I'll walk to your village', and `village_rescued_ranger` is already placed there by it. Mira is the one who would notice a stranger arrive. Carries the same `shop:goods:mira` effect every other Mira branch carries -- D39's rule, a vendor branch is never lost, only ever carried forward -- so this replaces her repeat-visit line for that window without costing the stall.

Says nothing the player has not already been told to their face: Sela says the seams are cut, in those words, in the conversation that sets this flag. Spec sec32's ladder is not moved and the legendary is not named.
village_mira_road.speaker: Mira
lines: Your surveyor walked in off the south road. Thin as a rake and asking for paper before she'd sit down.
She says the seams were cut. Cut, like a quarry face, by somebody, on purpose. I have lived under them my whole life and nobody has ever once said that out loud in this square.

lines.text: So take what you need and don't count it too carefully. I'd sooner be short of stock than short of you.

village_oskar_bridge._comment:
T5-STORY-2, and the same measured gap `village_mira_road` documents. Gated on `south_bridge_open` because the key that opens it was HIS -- his own `village_oskar_challenge` line already says so ('Tether took the key off my belt in the spring and put one of their own on the near landing'), and until now the game never let him find out it had come back. That is F3's 'returning is worth it' in one branch.

Carries `shop:creatures:oskar`, per D39, so the pen stays reachable. Placed above his `defeated_oskar` branch and below his `legendary_freed` one, so his challenge (which sits higher and is `unless defeated_oskar`) is untouched and the ending still wins.
village_oskar_bridge.speaker: Oskar
lines: The near landing's clear. Tam's boy ran the whole way back to tell me and he hasn't run anywhere since he was nine.
That was my key on that man's belt. They took it off me in the spring and I let them, because what was I going to do — and I have been quietly ashamed of it every day since.

lines.text: Pen's open. Take a proper look this time, and pick something that can stand still and take a hit. Whatever's up that road is not a grunt on a bridge.

village_tam_hall._comment:
T5-STORY-2, the third of the mid-chapter branches and deliberately the last one before the Hall. Gated on `hall_approach_open`, which `playground_world.gd` sets when all three captain sigils are in hand -- so this fires at the exact moment the player is equipped to walk at the stronghold and is the chapter's last chance for home to say goodbye. A smith is the one villager who would know a sigil on sight.

No effect: Tam has no vendor branch to carry (his own `_beaten` entry's `_why` says so -- both his gifts are one-time and long spent by here), so this is flavour, like that one. Nothing here names what is under the Hall; spec sec32's ladder holds.
village_tam_hall.speaker: Tam
lines: Three sigils. I've held one of those, once — a man came through buying nails and wouldn't say what for, and I've thought about it every year since.
Nobody carries three for any other reason. You're going to the Hall.
Then go the way you'd finish a weld. Rested, and all at once. Not tired, and not in pieces.

_comment_se30: SE30 (spec Sec32's reveal ladder, plus D41's own new rung). The ladder is: villagers know travel and trade are controlled AND that the ground near Team Tether's works is dying, without knowing why; the quarry shows conduits; the relay shows energy routed and an investigator held; the rescued captive knows the separation is MADE and that power runs toward the stronghold, and no further; the Upper Meadows shows the scale of it; and the stronghold, and nowhere before it, names the legendary as the source. The drain lines added to Mira/Tam/Oskar/the foreman are the rung D41 created and nobody had spoken: the world had 2737 painted pixels of dying ground and not one line of dialogue admitting it. Each speaker reports what their own trade would notice -- rows that won't take, creatures that won't den, seams that go bad, a verge that used to be waist high -- and none of them offers a cause. tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd::test_no_dialogue_before_the_stronghold_names_the_legendary enforces the top of the ladder across every dialogue file, not just the captive's.
_comment_tournament_1: TOURNAMENT-1. Oskar's challenge and beaten lines no longer promise the South Bridge Key: the 2026-08-22 owner directive moved the gatekeeper role to a Team Tether grunt so Oskar could be the tournament's final round. His words now point at the person who actually holds it, which is also how the player learns there is somebody standing at the crossing. His `shop:creatures:oskar` effect is untouched (D39: a vendor branch is never lost), and `tests/test_dialogue_runner.gd::test_both_of_oskars_branches_open_the_swap` still passes on it.
